verdicts.quote: "There are two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0."
verdicts.reason: Copper documents both API keys and OAuth2 and states OAuth2 is preferred for partner integrations, which is what a multi-tenant agent would use.

verdicts.quote: "Available on our trial, professional and business plan"
verdicts.reason: This shows developers can self‑serve credentials during the free trial (not paid-only). The paid tiers enable ongoing use, but initial access is self‑serve via the trial.

verdicts.quote: "Fetch a Lead by ID • Create a New Lead • Update a Lead • Delete a Lead"
verdicts.reason: The docs expose full CRUD on core objects and many areas (Leads, People, Companies, Opportunities, Projects, Tasks, Activities, Custom Fields, Files, Webhooks), indicating a broad API surface.

verdicts.quote: "Yes. Copper is launching an official MCP server, built and hosted by Copper. The beta launches in November 2026."
verdicts.reason: Vendor confirms an official, first‑party MCP server.
Buildable now, but caveats include manual OAuth app registration (not self‑serve) and plan gating for production use, so “ready_with_caveats” fits.
